evidence: Full lavaṇa gives Pali/Prakrit lavaṇa/lōṇa/lūṇa and the regional l/n-initial salt series, including Kalasha lṽŕ, Shina lōəṇ/lūəṇī, Bengali lon/lun/nūn and Marathi loṇ. These support retained lobon, reduced nasal-vowel forms, nwan/nʷãn/nõən and naṇ. Nasal loss or assimilation and local vowels remain qualified; both lobon/nun alternatives belong to this family. Cross-IA transmission is unresolved, not grounds for withholding the family link.

Full mṛṣṭa explicitly gives Marathi mīṭh and Konkani mīṭa salt alongside Gujarati mīṭhũ sweet. These support western miṭhu/mitu/miṭ salt responses, preserving source aspiration and ending differences and qualifying regional transmission. Do not use 10139 miṣṭa mixed: its full article has no salt evidence, despite a misleading parsed salt comparandum under it.

Full taila gives widespread tel/tēl oil, Oriya tela and northwestern reflexes. This supports telo, Dang ṭʲal and both Bshk tel/tāīl alternatives, preserving local vowels/palatalization with transmission qualified.

Full cikkaṇa gives Oriya cikaṇa/cikaṇā oil or ghee, Bihari ciknā oil seeds/ghee, Assamese sikaṇ smooth and Bengali cikan. Eastern cikən/cikon/cikoṇ/sikon oil responses fit this documented adjective-to-oil family; retain the local affricate/sibilant realization and qualify cross-IA transmission.
